query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A stepwise aging treatment that promotes the in situ formation of nanoscale, coherent precipitates along the lamellar colony interfaces will improve both the room‐temperature tensile strength and ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with dual-phase lamellar colonies having numerous, typically incoherent or weakly bonded internal boundaries that act as microcrack initiation sites during tensile deformation.
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled post-solidification heat treatment (aged in two steps) designed to induce the precipitation of coherent nanoprecipitates along the lamellar interfaces.
generation.conditions: Aging at an intermediate temperature (below the melting point) for a specified duration that is optimized to generate nanoscale precipitates without causing coarsening; subsequent room-temperature tensile testing.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of nanoscale coherent precipitates (analogous to δ-lamellae and γ″ particles seen in related refractory HEAs) distributed along the lamellar interfaces.
generation.mechanism: The coherent precipitates modify the interfacial character by reducing stress concentrations and facilitating homogeneous dislocation motion (via a combination of dislocation shearing and pinning) across the lamellar boundaries. This mitigates premature microcrack initiation while contributing to precipitation strengthening.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the unmodified lamellar baseline, the treated alloy is expected to exhibit an increased ultimate tensile strength (by the order of ~1 GPa as seen in similar systems) and improved tensile elongation, with fewer internal cracks initiating under room-temperature loading.
generation.baseline: As-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with dual-phase lamellar colonies that exhibit microcrack-triggered catastrophic failure during room-temperature tensile deformation.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is expected only when the alloy composition is conducive to forming coherent precipitates and the aging parameters (temperature and duration) are within a window that avoids overaging or precipitate coarsening. Too high a temperature or too long a treatment may lead to incoherent, coarse precipitates that do not enhance ductility.
generation.uncertainty: Precise aging temperatures, times, and the quantitative extent of improvements in strength and ductility require experimental optimization; the predicted magnitude of performance gains (e.g., ~1 GPa strength increase) is based on analogous systems and may vary with composition and processing specifics.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of eutectic high-entropy alloy specimens: one set processed by conventional casting (serving as the baseline) and another set subjected to the proposed stepwise aging treatment. Characterize the microstructures using transmission electron microscopy and electron backscatter diffraction to confirm the formation, size, and coherence of the nanoscale precipitates along lamellar interfaces. Perform room-temperature uniaxial tensile tests on both sets to compare the ultimate tensile strength, ductility, and fracture characteristics.
measurements: Precipitate size, distribution, and interface coherence (via TEM/EBSD)
Fractography to assess microcrack initiation sites
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aging treatment does not result in statistically significant improvements in both tensile strength and ductility, or if it leads to increased or unchanged microcrack formation compared to the conventional baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.
